sections.history: Dharmapuram, near Karaikal in the Kaveri delta, is an ancient Shaiva village hymned in the seventh-century Tevaram by Sambandar and counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams. The stone temple is of the Chola period with later additions. Its great distinction is its link to Tiru Neelakanta Yazhpanar, one of the sixty-three Nayanmars and the foremost yazh-player of the Tevaram age, whose family belonged to this place and who travelled with Sambandar, rendering the saint's hymns on his lute.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Dravidian plan with a gopuram, prakara and the sanctum of Yazhmoorinathar. Its iconography and tradition keep alive the music of the yazh and the memory of Yazhpanar, so that the shrine is cherished as much by lovers of Tamil music and the Tevaram as by local devotees. The name of the lord, Yazhmoorinathar, keeps the instrument at the heart of the temple's identity.
sections.legends: The temple's defining tradition is the Yazh Muri Pathigam. Tiru Neelakanta Yazhpanar accompanied Sambandar on his yazh; but when Sambandar sang a hymn on Ganesha whose depth the yazh could not fully capture, the player, unwilling to offer anything less than the hymn deserved, resolved to break his beloved instrument — and was gently stopped, the saint affirming that his music was worthy. A second tradition ties the lord's name to Yama, who worshipped here after the Markandeya episode and was told his curse would in time be lifted; and another recalls Yudhishtira worshipping here in the Pandavas' exile.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Shaiva festival calendar — Maha Shivaratri, Pradosham, the Margazhi season and the annual Brahmotsavam. The association with Yazhpanar gives the days honouring the Nayanmars a special resonance, and the temple is remembered wherever the story of the yazh and the Tevaram is told.
sections.experience: Dharmapuram offers the pilgrim a temple bound to music and devotion — the place of the great yazh-player who would break his lute rather than fall short of a hymn. The darshan of Yazhmoorinathar carries this sense of art offered wholly to the divine, and for lovers of the Tevaram it is a shrine of particular tenderness.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Dharmapuram is near Karaikal (Puducherry), close to the Nagapattinam/Mayiladuthurai border, roughly 5-6 km from Karaikal town; the nearest rail heads are Karaikal and Nagore, with local buses and taxis to the temple.
